p.title: Dadi's missing glasses
p.challenge: Put the funny story of Dadi's glasses in order. Find the surprise at the end!
panels: Dadi could not find her glasses.
She looked under the sofa and behind the TV.
She even looked in Bholu the cat's basket.
'Who has hidden my glasses?' she cried.
Tara giggled and pointed: the glasses were on a mango!
Dadi had put them there herself. The whole family laughed.

p.title: Masculine, feminine or both?
p.challenge: Sort each family word: does it name a male, a female, or can it be used for both?

items.why: A parent's brother is an uncle: masculine.
A parent's sister is an aunt: feminine.
A brother's or sister's son: masculine.
A brother's or sister's daughter: feminine.
A cousin can be a boy or a girl.

p.title: Gone with the scooter
p.challenge: Put the scooter adventure in order: the trip, the problem, and how it was solved
panels: Chachu and I rode to the lake on his old red scooter.
On the way, the scooter began to cough and splutter.
It stopped near a sugarcane field!
We pushed it along the road for a long time.
A kind farmer gave us water and showed us a repair shop.
By evening we reached the lake, tired but very happy.

p.title: The Rainbow (poem)
p.challenge: Put the lines of the rainbow poem in order. Listen for the rhymes: new–hue, bright–light, too–you
panels: After the rain, the sky is new,
A shining bow of every hue.
Red and orange, yellow bright,
Green and blue in golden light,
Indigo and violet too,
A painted bridge for me and you!

p.title: Mithu, the wise parrot
p.challenge: Put the folk tale of Mithu in order. What does Mithu ask for at the end?
panels: Long ago, a king kept a parrot, Mithu, in a silver cage.
The king asked a riddle: "What grows the more you share it?"
No minister could answer.
Mithu called out, "Happiness, Your Majesty!"
The pleased king said, "Ask for any reward."
Mithu asked: "Please open my cage and let me fly."
The king kept his word. Mithu visits as a free friend.

p.title: Synonyms or antonyms?
p.challenge: Is each word pair a synonym pair (same meaning) or an antonym pair (opposite)?

items.why: The cage was shut, but now it is open.

p.challenge: Join the two ideas with the best joining word: and, but, because, so or or

items.from: The parrot was clever. It won its freedom.
items.text: The parrot was clever, so it won its freedom.
items.hint: The second idea is a RESULT of the first.

items.from: The cage was pretty. Mithu wanted to be free.
items.text: The cage was pretty, but Mithu wanted to be free.
items.hint: The second idea is a CONTRAST (something different).

items.from: Mithu was happy. The cage was open.
items.text: Mithu was happy because the cage was open.
items.hint: The second idea gives the REASON.

items.from: The king smiled. The queen smiled.
items.text: The king and the queen smiled.
items.hint: We ADD one person to the other.

items.from: Would you like a guava? Would you like a chilli?
items.text: Would you like a guava or a chilli?
items.hint: You can have only one: it is a CHOICE.

p.title: What a tank!
p.challenge: Put the story in order: the problem, its cause, and the lesson the children learnt
panels: One hot May morning, the taps in Gully No. 4 went dry.
"The tank on the roof is empty!" shouted Bunty.
A pipe had been leaking all night: drip, drip, drip.
A plumber fixed the pipe.
A water tanker came at noon.
The children made a poster: "Every drop counts!"

p.title: Compound words
p.challenge: Join two words into one compound word, and split compound words back into their two parts — 5 right
pairs: rain + water = water from the rain
water + fall = water falling from a height
water + melon = a big, juicy fruit
tooth + brush = a brush for teeth
bath + room = a room for bathing
roof + top = the top of the roof
tea + pot = a pot for making tea
butter + fly: a new meaning! A butterfly is not made of butter.

p.title: Gilli danda after school
p.challenge: Put Irfan and Gopal's game of gilli danda in order
panels: After school, Irfan and Gopal raced to the open ground.
Gopal tapped one end of the gilli and it flew up.
Whack! He hit it far across the ground with the danda.
Irfan ran and caught it. "Out!" he laughed.
They took turns and played till sunset.
Then they walked home together, still laughing.

items.hint: between = in the middle of two

items.text: He hit the gilli across the ground.
items.hint: across = from one side to the other

p.title: The Decision of the Panchayat
p.challenge: Put the story in order. Why was "Let the calf choose" a fair test?
panels: Harish and Anil both said a lost calf was theirs.
They went to the panchayat.
The Sarpanch listened to both of them calmly.
She said, "Let the calf choose."
The calf ran straight to Anil's cow to drink milk.
Harish said sorry, and the two farmers shook hands.

p.challenge: Make 6 opposites of fairness words with the prefixes un-, dis- and in-
Write what people said: add speech marks, commas, capitals and end marks
items: The Sarpanch said, "Let the calf choose."
"The calf belongs to Anil," said the Sarpanch.

p.title: Vocation (poem)
p.challenge: Put the lines of the poem in order. Each pair rhymes: bread–shed, wheat–street, tall–all
panels: I watch the baker knead the bread,
I watch the painter paint the shed.
The farmer sows the seeds of wheat,
The postman cycles down our street.
I wonder, when I'm grown and tall,
Which one I'll be, or maybe all!
